name: Chiffon cake
origin: Invented by Harry Baker, a Los Angeles insurance salesman, in 1927, and sold to General Mills in 1947; the first American cake to use vegetable oil rather than a solid fat, giving a crumb that stays moist after cooling.

ingredients.note: chiffon's defining ingredient is a liquid oil, not a solid fat; packages/data/substances has no vegetable-oil record yet (see catalog.ts module notes), so this line cannot yet move real mass through a Ledger

real chiffon uses baking powder (bicarbonate plus its own dry acid partner); modelled as bicarbonate alone, the same representative simplification leavening.ts already uses for chemical leavening generally

process.name: combine wet ingredients
process.description: whisk oil, egg yolks, water and half the sugar with the sifted flour, baking powder and salt into a smooth batter

process.name: whip egg whites
process.description: whip egg whites to soft peaks, adding the remaining sugar gradually to a stable meringue

process.name: fold together
process.description: fold the meringue into the batter in stages

process.name: bake
process.description: bake in an ungreased tube pan so the batter can climb the sides, then cool inverted

notes: Ratios follow the standard chiffon proportion (Gisslen, Professional Baking): oil around 35-45% of flour, egg around 150% (yolks in the batter, whipped whites folded in separately), water around 40-60%, sugar slightly above flour. Effective hydration (~154% of flour, crediting egg's own water) sits inside the engine's real cake-batter band and below the ~180% ceiling documented in formulation.ts, consistent with chiffon's real reputation as one of the wettest standard American layer-cake batters.
